title: Harden kernel-path decision tree after attention-sparsity experiment caused p95 regression
creator: Anita Kapoor
body: Summary: A staged experiment enabling an attention-sparsity optimization flag (sparsitize-attn-v2) caused intermittent p95 latency regressions for multi-turn chat workloads with 512-1024 token sequences. The issue manifested as sporadic kernel path flips at microbatch boundaries which increased descheduled recompile and KV-cache-warmup costs, amplifying tail latency under medium concurrency (30-80 qps). This ticket captures timeline, root-cause, immediate mitigations, and a prioritized action plan to harden the kernel-path decision logic and prevent similar regressions.
timeline:
2025-01-16 09:12 UTC: Canary rollout of sparsitize-attn-v2 to 10% of runtime capacity enabled via feature flag.
2025-01-16 11:03 UTC: Observability spike: p95 latency from 55ms -> 220ms on canary nodes serving seq_len 512-1024 requests. Alert routed to on-call infra runtime team.
2025-01-16 11:07 UTC: Immediate mitigation: rollback flag to previous safe config; canary traffic reverted.
2025-01-16 11:30-13:00 UTC: Triaging: correlation found between kernel_path choice change (fused-attn vs dequant-attn) and requests that had a mixture of cached KV prefixes from prior short-context requests.
2025-01-16 14:15 UTC: Reproduced locally in synthetic harness using interleaved short (32 tokens) followed by long (768 tokens) sequences; observed kernel recompile and cache-warm start-ups when path selection changed mid-session.
2025-01-17 - 01-20: Deep dive with serving runtime, scheduler, and attention teams. Hypothesis solidified: the path selector used a short-window scoring signal (recent throughput/latency samples) and an experimental sparsity score; under workload shifts the selector flips path aggressively without hysteresis, causing microbatch evictions and kernel recompile thrash.
2025-01-21: Hotfix rolled: add temporary path-lock per-connection for 5 seconds and increase score smoothing window to 30s to mitigate flips. Hotfix deployed to canary and then to production; observed p95 returned to baseline in controlled tests.
root_cause: The kernel-path decision tree weighted a new attention-sparsity signal too highly without adequate hysteresis and without considering per-connection KV cache affinity. Under mixed short-then-long sequence patterns, the selector would switch from a low-latency fused-attn kernel to a quantized dequant path (and vice versa) between adjacent microbatches. That switch triggered kernel module reinitialization and KV cache warmups, producing tail latency amplification. Additionally, the scheduler admitted microbatches assuming stable kernel affinity which resulted in inefficient packing and temporary starvation when paths flipped.
reproduction_steps:
1) Start synthetic serving harness with a model that supports both fused-attn and quant/dequant paths (replicating model variant used in canary).
2) Configure harness to send interleaved requests: 10 requests of length 32 tokens followed by 20 requests of length 768 tokens; repeat pattern at 50 qps.
3) Enable the experimental sparsitize-attn-v2 scoring in the path decision component.
4) Observe kernel selection logs for connection X: toggling between 'fused-attn' and 'dequant-attn' within a session and increased kernel_init and kv_warmup counters.
5) Measure tail latencies; should reproduce p95 spikes similar to canary.
Notes: reproduction requires same microbatching settings and scheduler admission thresholds as production (microbatch_size=8, admission_window=100ms).
mitigations:
Immediate actions taken: rollback the experimental flag from production; deployed path-lock hotfix (per-connection sticky selection for 5s) and expanded smoothing window for scoring from 5s -> 30s. Observed stabilization in canary.
Short-term hardening: keep path-lock in place; add an emergency circuit that rejects path switches if KV cache warmup_count > 0 or kernel_init_count increased in last 1 minute.
Long-term: implement a robust scoring redesign (see action items) and strengthen scheduler awareness of kernel affinity to avoid packing microbatches across conflicting kernel paths.
action_items: A1: Implement 3-tier scoring with affinity bias: factor in (a) per-connection KV affinity score, (b) 60s exponential smoothing of latency and throughput metrics, and (c) explicit experiment weight caps. Owner: Marco Santos. Estimate: 5. Due: 2025-02-08.
A2: Add hysteresis and minimum-commit-duration to path selection: default 30s or N requests whichever longer; make this configurable per-model. Owner: Priya Nair. Estimate: 3. Due: 2025-02-05.

A3: Scheduler change to tag microbatches with intended kernel_path and preferentially pack compatible microbatches; reject admission if packing would mix >1 kernel_path in same work unit. Owner: Ethan Liu. Estimate: 5. Due: 2025-02-12.

A4: Extend telemetry to emit kernel_init_count, kv_warmup_count, and path_switch_rate per-connection into metrics backend and create alert thresholds for path_switch_rate > 2/min for high-seq workloads. Owner: SRE — Rina Gomez. Estimate: 2. Due: 2025-01-30.
A5: Create synthetic regression suite for mixed-length session patterns and add to CI canary gating; include per-version p95/p99 baselines. Owner: QA — Omar El-Amin. Estimate: 4. Due: 2025-02-01.

A6: Review experiment rollout procedures: require runtime-team signoff when experiments change kernel-scoring signals and add automated canary load shapes emulating mixed-length sessions. Owner: Product — Laura Chen. Estimate: 2. Due: 2025-01-28.

A7: Postmortem doc & stakeholder notification: notify enterprise customers who observed increased latency; prepare FAQ and CS playbook. Owner: Customer Success — Dalia Hossain. Estimate: 1. Due: 2025-01-25.

2025-01-17 Priya Nair: Confirmed reproduction in local harness using mixed-length pattern. Sending proposal for hysteresis changes.
2025-01-18 Rina Gomez: Added provisional alerts and dashboard panels for kernel_init_count and kv_warmup_count.
2025-01-20 Anita Kapoor: Customer impact assessment sent to CS — two enterprise tenants reported spikes during canary window.

2025-01-28 Laura Chen: Updated rollout checklist to include mixed-session canary step; will require product signoff for future kernel-affecting experiments.
followup_notes:
We observed that several historical regression events share the same pattern: score-based rapid switching + cache affinity mismatch. Consider creating a generic 'affinity-safety' framework that runtime experiments must opt-into before being allowed to change kernel scoring weights. Track compliance as part of experiment governance.
Also discuss introducing a low-overhead per-connection sticky token in protocol so downstream schedulers and runtime can coordinate packing without global locks.
